Reading the list

What each column
is telling you

Location is the city or settlement the airport serves, which is not always the name on the terminal. The airport serving Bergamo is called Orio al Serio, the one serving Frankfurt at distance is called Hahn, and travellers who book on the city name alone occasionally land a long way from where they meant to be.

Airport is the official name. IATA is the three letter commercial code you see on a ticket. ICAO is the four letter operational code used on flight plans, unique worldwide and structured by region. Some entries show no IATA code because none has ever been assigned, which is common at airfields with no scheduled service and no obstacle at all to a private flight.

Book tells you whether we publish a full guide to that airport, covering runways, elevation, operating hours, private terminals, transfer times and typical private jet charter pricing. If there is no guide, ask anyway. The guides reflect what we are asked about most, not the limits of where we fly.

Airport codes are the fastest way to be certain you are talking about the same place. Two cities can share a name, two airports can share a city, and a booking made on a city name alone can put you an hour from where you meant to be. Quoting the airport code removes the ambiguity, which is why every private jet charter enquiry we handle is confirmed against a code rather than a name.

Using the list well

  • The filter at the top searches every column at once, so a country name, a city, an airport name or either code all work.
  • It tolerates missing accents. Type Zurich or Malaga and the right entry still appears.
  • Use the region buttons to jump, then the country links inside each region to go straight to a table.
  • A city with several airports usually has a quieter one that is better for private travel and closer to where you are going.
  • An airport in this list is not automatically one you can fly into internationally. Customs availability is a separate question.
The list tells you an airport exists. Whether you can land there depends on runway, hours, permits and customs.

From a code in the list
to an aircraft on the ramp

If you know the airport, the searchable directory is the faster way to look one up, and the guide to airports of entry explains which of these fields can clear an international arrival and how much notice each country needs. If you know the journey rather than the airport, the route directory prices thousands of city pairs, and empty legs lists the same aircraft repositioning at a fraction of the usual figure.

For anything else, ask. Give us the airport code or simply the address you are trying to reach, the date and the number of passengers, and you get back the right aircraft, the right field and one fixed all-in private jet charter price.

List questions

Codes,
columns and coverage, answered

How many airports are on this page?

7,274 airports across 239 countries and territories, grouped by country within six regions.

Why do some airports show no IATA code?

IATA codes are assigned for commercial purposes, so airfields with no scheduled service often have none. They still hold an ICAO code and can usually accept private aircraft.

What is the difference between the Location and Airport columns?

Location is the city the airport serves. Airport is its official name, which is frequently different. Bergamo is served by Orio al Serio, and booking on a city name alone can land you a long way from where you meant to be.

Can I search this page?

Yes. The filter at the top searches country, city, airport name, IATA and ICAO together, and it hides everything that does not match so you can see the result in context.

Does the filter handle accents?

Yes. Type Zurich, Malaga or Dusseldorf without the accents and the correct entry still appears.

What does the Guide button mean?

It means we publish a full guide to that airport with runways, elevation, operating hours, private terminals, transfer times and typical charter prices. There are 181 of them and the number grows.

Can you fly to an airport with no guide?

Yes. The guides cover the airports we are asked about most, not the limits of where we fly. Ask about any field on this list and you will get an answer, usually within the hour.

Does an airport being listed mean a private jet can land there?

No. It confirms the airport exists and gives its codes. Whether you can land depends on runway length for your aircraft, operating hours, slots, permits and, for international arrivals, customs availability.

Which airport should I pick when a city has several?

Usually the one closest to your actual address that can take your aircraft and clear your arrival. That is rarely the airport with the famous name, and the time saved on the ground is often larger than any difference in the air.

How is the list ordered?

By region, then alphabetically by country, then alphabetically by the city each airport serves.

Is this list only international airports?

No. It includes every airport in our database, international and domestic. Whether a given field can process an international arrival is covered in our guide to airports of entry.

How often is it updated?

It is maintained alongside our airport guides and route database. If you find an entry that has changed, closed or moved, tell us and we will correct it.
